title: A computer that ran on water
facts: The MONIAC was a real analog computer that used water moving through tanks, pipes and valves to model money flows in an economy.
Changing valves represented changes in economic policy.
People built the machine; water inside it performed the calculations.
cautions: Electronic computers already existed. Do not claim this predicted the future, was the first computer, or existed before computers.

title: The record we sent into space
facts: Both Voyager spacecraft carry a gold-plated phonograph record containing sounds and images from Earth.
The records include music, natural sounds and spoken greetings in 55 languages.
The protective cover carries symbolic instructions explaining how to play the record and locate Earth.
cautions: The record travels outward with the spacecraft; it was not sent back to Earth. It is a message intended for a possible finder, not a discovered alien artifact. Do not claim anybody has received or played it.

title: An ancient machine that tracked the sky
facts: The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek geared device recovered from a shipwreck.
It used interlocking gears and dials for astronomical and calendar calculations.
Researchers determined that its mechanisms could predict solar and lunar eclipses.
cautions: This was an analog astronomical calculator, not a modern electronic or general-purpose computer. Do not invent a precise age, discovery date, or number of gears.
